title: ropeway:handbook-title-51
text: Two finished towers become a span. Right-click a finished tower's footing and pick the tower to link to from the list, which shows the distance, the rope each link will cost, and how much haul rope you are carrying. Only towers that can actually be linked appear, so nothing in that list can fail when you click it. Rows you cannot afford are marked [!] and are still listed, so you know what to go and craft. Rope cost One haul rope per four blocks of span, rounded up when you build and rounded down when you break. A 30.4-block span costs 8 and refunds 7. That loss of at most one rope per span is deliberate - splicing wastes rope. Haul rope stacks to 16, so a long span is paid for out of several stacks at once. Spans are measured sheave to sheave, four blocks above the footings you clicked - so two towers on level ground are exactly as far apart as they look. Limits - Longest single span: 48 blocks. - Longest whole line: 320 blocks. - A tower carries at most two spans, so a line is a chain, never a junction. What blocks a span The cabin needs a clear three-wide tube along the whole span, running from the rope line down past the bottom of the cabin - the cabin hangs a little over two blocks under the rope, so a rise that clears the rope can still be in the cabin's way. Leaves and plants do not block it - a ropeway through the canopy is fine. Anything solid does. The four blocks at each end are not checked, because that is where the towers' own posts stand. If a span is later walled off, the cabin holds at the tower before it rather than dragging you into stone. Riding Right-click an end tower's footing holding the ropeway cabin to hang it on the line. A line takes one cabin. Sit down and it departs after about three seconds, runs at a little over two blocks a second, and holds at the far tower until someone boards for the return trip. Look around freely the whole way, or press the ropeway outside view key - Ropeway: outside view while riding in Settings > Controls - to watch the cabin from outside as it runs, and again to come back inside. It only does anything while you are aboard, and your own camera comes back when you get off. Choosing where you get off Left alone, a ride runs all the way to the end of the line and passes straight through every tower in between. To get off sooner, press the ropeway stop key while you are aboard - it is listed as Ropeway: ask for a stop in Settings > Controls, and the cabin tells you the key it is bound to in chat as you sit down. The cabin answers in chat with the tower it will stop at, and it stops there. Press it again before you arrive and the selection steps on to the next tower, and the one after that, and past the end of the line it comes back round the other way - which is also how you leave an interior tower in the direction the cabin is not already pointing. Pressing it while parked departs at once instead of waiting out the boarding pause. You can only get on and off while the cabin is stopped at a tower. Standing on the ground at a tower the cabin floor rides a block above the ground - about waist height on a standing player, not over your head - so step aside or crouch when one is coming through. Carrying freight A ropeway was built to move goods, and the cabin does. Each of its two benches is also a cargo bay: hold a basket, Ctrl and right-click the bench, and it is strapped down there. Right-click a loaded bench - no modifier - to open it and put things in or take them out, from inside the cabin or standing beside it. Ctrl and right-click with an empty hand takes the container back off, and like every mount in the game it has to be emptied before it will come off. A loaded bench cannot be sat on. So a cabin carries two loads, or one load and one passenger, and never two of each - freight and people compete for the same two seats, exactly as they did on the real thing. A basket holds eight kinds of thing, so a full cabin is sixteen. Baskets are the only container that fits: a crate has no dialog on a mount at all - a click takes one thing out at a time - and a chest is sixteen mixed slots, and a gondola is not a warehouse. The cargo rides with the cabin: it survives leaving the chunk, saving, and a server restart, and it does not slow the cabin down or change what it costs to run. If the cabin is ever removed - the last tower of its line broken, or the span it hangs on cut - everything comes back. The goods come out of the containers, the emptied containers come back too, and the cabin item with them; whatever does not fit in your inventory falls at the cabin's feet. Nothing is destroyed, but a loaded cabin taken down does leave a pile to pick up, so unload before you dismantle a line. Calling the cabin Every finished tower on a line is a station, not only the two ends. Right-click any footing with an empty hand and an empty cabin comes to that tower and stops there, so a long line is a row of stops rather than a shuttle between its ends. Calling needs the cabin to be empty; from inside it, the stop key does the same job. Look at a footing to read whether the cabin is standing there, on its way to it, or elsewhere on the line. Ctrl and right-click opens the linking and naming list instead. Taking it down Breaking a pylon footing refunds the rope of its spans, unlinks the towers on the other side, and removes the rope. It is refused outright while someone is riding that line. If that leaves the line with no spans at all, the cabin comes down with it and the cabin item is handed back to you. Breaking a post or the pylon head just makes the tower incomplete; the spans survive until the footing goes. Corners A tower faces one of four directions; the cabin follows the rope. When it stops at a tower it turns to sit square to that tower - flush across the crossarm, parallel to the posts - rather than staying angled at wherever it is going next, so you board and step off a cabin that is straight in its station, and it swings back onto the line as it leaves. While it is moving it follows the rope and nothing else: where a line changes direction at a tower the cabin cuts the corner, and it can clip a post. It cannot hurt you, and nothing you build stops it. Gentle corners are fine - up to about thirty degrees the cabin misses the posts entirely, and the wide archway is there to give it that room. Sharper than that and it starts to catch them. At a right angle the cabin passes straight through a post, every time: a tower can only face north, south, east or west, so at ninety degrees the outgoing rope runs along the very line its own posts stand on, and there is nowhere else for the cabin to be. That is the shape of the tower, not a fault - it will not be fixed, so build around it. Turn a line with two or three gentle towers rather than one sharp one, and face each footing down its own line - the block info panel names the two directions before you build anything.
